slides.text: When Kevin from Marketing broke his collarbone during a gentle spin class, Arthur in Accounts sent him a modest potted succulent and a get-well card. Not to be outdone, Brenda from Human Resources countered with a three-tiered artisan fruit basket imported from Sicily. Sensing a direct assault on his workplace status, Arthur retaliated by hiring a four-piece string quartet to perform outside Kevin's bedroom window at seven in the morning.

By Thursday, Kevin’s modest two-bedroom bungalow had become ground zero for competitive corporate empathy. Brenda dispatched a mobile wood-fired pizza truck that parked directly across his driveway, while Arthur countered by having a certified Zen master install a seven-hundred-pound bubbling travertine fountain in Kevin's living room. Kevin, who only wanted to nap on painkillers, barricaded his hallway in sheer panic as delivery couriers began brawling on his lawn over parking privileges.

The warfare reached its zenith on Friday when Brenda arrived leading a licensed emotional-support alpaca wearing a tailored silk necktie. Arthur was already waiting on the front porch with a notarized deed gifting Kevin forty percent ownership of a boutique lavender farm. Kevin finally stepped onto the porch in his sling and cleared his throat. 'Guys,' he whispered, terrified, 'I'm feeling much better. Please, for the love of God, take the alpaca.'
